newsitem.title: SPAIN: GOLF - MCNULTY MOVES INTO BIG MASTERS LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF - MCNULTY MOVES INTO BIG MASTERS LEAD.

text.p: Zimbabwean veteran Mark McNulty survived a birthday celebration on Friday night to secure a four-shot lead with a bogey-free four-under-par third round of 67 in the Volvo Masters on Saturday.
McNulty, 43 on Friday, carried his celebration onto the course as the overnight contenders and bigger names failed to get to grips with the punishing 6,819-yard Valderrama layout.
"This course treats players with no respect, but I had one of those days when I was always in the right position," McNulty said.
"It was what I'd call a great round of golf. I made some birdies and holed a few putts for par. But I never like to count the chickens until they arrive."

McNulty's round took him to five under par for 54 holes, four clear of a group of six players including Jose Coceres of Argentina who put together an improbable round of 18 successive pars for his 71.

Those tied with him were Frank Nobilo of New Zealand after a 70 that contained a bogey six at the watery and devilish 17th hole, Australian Wayne Riley after a 69 and Britons Lee Westwood and Gary Orr with 70s and Aldrew Oldcorn with a 72.
Overnight leader Paul Curry of Britain plunged out of contention 10 shots behind McNulty with a 10-over-par 81 that included an eight at the 17th.
Trinidad's Stephen Ames, second overnight, had a six there in a 77.
That hole came in for severe criticism last year and again on Saturday, especially for a pin position on the right front of the green just beyond a severe slope back into a lake.
"The course is hard enough without that," said Colin Montgomerie, European number one for a fourth successive year. He shot a level-par 71 and is nine behind McNulty.
Nobilo said the hole was unfair while Bernhard Langer still dislikes the humps on the landing area of the fairway after he took seven when his third shot found a lake.
"I hit a perfect drive and had 210 yards to the front of the green and had no shot because my drive finished on a downslope and I would not have been able to get it airborne," he said.
"I'd have designed it differently," added the German, who hit a pitching wedge second shot short of the lake and a lob wedge to the green that spun back down the slope into the water.

His 74 left him with a three-over par 216 total, eight shots behind McNulty and with virtually no chance of adding to his record of at least one European Tour title every year for 16 successive years. He has not won this year.
Nobilo's compatriot Greg Turner is alone on level par after a 71 including a birdie four at the 17th.
"I think it's a terrible hole anyway and the pin position compounds it.
"You shouldn't have a pin position that leads to a three-shot swing," Turner said.
McNulty was in the minority who did not disapprove after playing his second shot with a wedge to leave himself a full nine iron to the green.
"Wherever the pin is, you know what you are in for. I didn't think it was unfair," he said.
His birdies came on good approaches, to four feet at the first, 10 feet at the long fourth, a wedge to two inches at the 10th and to six feet at the 11th.
"I won't be thinking of winning," he said. "I tend when I'm playing decent to try and concentrate on the job at hand, not think what could or might happen."

McNulty, who still has trouble with his right knee, where the joint became infected during 1995, said he celebrated on Friday with Nobilo and South African David Frost by drinking three bottles of 1985 rioja, a Spanish red wine.
He credited his fine showing to a more measured schedule than many other players have had.
"I've played just 17 tournaments this year, only 13 in Europe," said the Zimbabwean, who won the Dimension Data pro-am European Tour event in South African in February and the Dutch Open in July.
"Some guys come here having played 30 tournaments but I've paced myself this year. I feel relatively fresh," he said.
